description: A study of the earth modelled as a sphere, covering latitude and longitude, great and small circles, and calculating distances along meridians and parallels of latitude in kilometres and nautical miles.

mcq.questionText: What is the latitude of the equator?
mcq.explanation: The equator is the reference circle from which latitude is measured north and south, so its latitude is 0 degrees. Exam Tip: latitude is always measured starting from the equator at 0 degrees.

mcq.questionText: A(30 degrees N, 40 degrees E) and B(45 degrees N, 40 degrees E) lie on the same meridian. What is the latitude difference?
mcq.explanation: Both points are north of the equator, so subtract the latitudes: 45 - 30 = 15 degrees. Exam Tip: when both places are on the same side of the equator, subtract.

mcq.questionText: P(20 degrees N, 35 degrees E) and Q(30 degrees S, 35 degrees E) lie on the same meridian. What is the latitude difference?
mcq.explanation: The points are on opposite sides of the equator, so add the latitudes: 20 + 30 = 50 degrees. Exam Tip: when places are on opposite sides of the equator, add.

mcq.questionText: What is the longitude difference between (10 degrees S, 40 degrees E) and (10 degrees S, 75 degrees E)?
mcq.explanation: Both longitudes are east of the prime meridian, so subtract: 75 - 40 = 35 degrees. Exam Tip: same side (both E or both W) means subtract.

mcq.questionText: What is the longitude difference between (5 degrees N, 20 degrees W) and (5 degrees N, 30 degrees E)?
mcq.explanation: The longitudes are on opposite sides of the prime meridian, so add: 20 + 30 = 50 degrees. Exam Tip: opposite sides (one E and one W) means add.

mcq.questionText: Two towns lie on the same meridian with a latitude difference of 30 degrees. What is the distance between them in km? (Take 2 x pi x R = 40,040 km)
mcq.explanation: Distance along a meridian = (theta/360) x 2 x pi x R = (30/360) x 40,040 = 3,336.7 km. Exam Tip: for meridian distance in km, use (latitude difference / 360) x 40,040.

mcq.questionText: Two points on the same great circle subtend 25 degrees at the centre of the earth. What is the distance between them in nautical miles?
mcq.explanation: One degree of arc on a great circle equals 60 nautical miles, so 25 x 60 = 1,500 nautical miles. Exam Tip: nautical mile distance on a great circle = 60 x angle in degrees.

mcq.questionText: What is the longitude of the Greenwich (prime) meridian?
mcq.explanation: The Greenwich or prime meridian is the reference line from which longitude is measured east and west, so its longitude is 0 degrees. Exam Tip: longitude is measured starting from the prime meridian at 0 degrees.

mcq.questionText: What is the radius of the circle of latitude 60 degrees N? (Take R = 6,370 km)
mcq.explanation: The radius of a parallel of latitude is R cos theta = 6,370 x cos 60 = 6,370 x 0.5 = 3,185 km. Exam Tip: the radius of a parallel of latitude equals R cos(latitude).

mcq.questionText: Two towns on latitude 60 degrees N have longitudes differing by 40 degrees. What is the distance along the parallel in km? (Take 2 x pi x R = 40,040 km)
mcq.explanation: Distance along a parallel = (longitude difference / 360) x 40,040 x cos theta = (40/360) x 40,040 x cos 60 = 2,224.4 km. Exam Tip: parallel distance in km includes the factor cos(latitude).

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a great circle?
mcq.explanation: A great circle has the same centre and radius as the earth; the equator is the only parallel of latitude that is a great circle. Exam Tip: among parallels of latitude, only the equator is a great circle.

mcq.questionText: A ship covers 1 nautical mile in one hour. What is its speed?
mcq.explanation: A speed of one nautical mile per hour is defined as one knot. Exam Tip: knot means nautical miles per hour, not km per hour.

mcq.questionText: A ship sails due north from (10 degrees S, 30 degrees E) through 20 degrees. What is its new position?
mcq.explanation: Sailing north, the ship first covers 10 degrees to reach the equator, then a further 10 degrees north, ending at 10 degrees N with the same longitude 30 degrees E. Exam Tip: sailing north or south changes only the latitude; watch for crossing the equator.

mcq.questionText: Two towns on latitude 60 degrees N differ in longitude by 30 degrees. What is the distance between them in nautical miles?
mcq.explanation: Distance along a parallel in nautical miles = 60 x longitude difference x cos theta = 60 x 30 x cos 60 = 60 x 30 x 0.5 = 900 nautical miles. Exam Tip: for a parallel, multiply 60 x longitude difference by cos(latitude).

mcq.questionText: A point lies on the equator at longitude 40 degrees E. How is its position written?
mcq.explanation: Position is written as (latitude, longitude), so on the equator (latitude 0 degrees) at longitude 40 degrees E it is (0 degrees, 40 degrees E). Exam Tip: always write latitude first, then longitude.

fib.questionText: The commonly used value for the radius of the earth is ____ km.
fib.explanation: The standard value taken for the radius of the earth in these calculations is R = 6,370 km. Exam Tip: remember R = 6,370 km, which gives 2 x pi x R = 40,040 km.

fib.questionText: The latitude of the North Pole is ____.
fib.explanation: Latitude increases from 0 degrees at the equator to 90 degrees at the poles, so the North Pole is at 90 degrees N. Exam Tip: the poles are at the maximum latitude of 90 degrees N or 90 degrees S.

fib.questionText: One nautical mile is the arc of a great circle subtending an angle of one ____ at the centre.
fib.explanation: A nautical mile is defined as the length of an arc of a great circle that subtends one minute of arc at the centre of the earth. Exam Tip: one degree = 60 minutes, so one degree of arc = 60 nautical miles.

fib.questionText: All parallels of latitude are small circles except the ____.
fib.explanation: Parallels of latitude are small circles because their centres do not coincide with the earth's centre; only the equator has the same centre and radius as the earth, making it a great circle. Exam Tip: the equator is the only parallel that is a great circle.

fib.questionText: The longitude difference between (15 degrees N, 50 degrees E) and (15 degrees N, 50 degrees W) is ____.
fib.explanation: The longitudes are on opposite sides of the prime meridian, so add them: 50 + 50 = 100 degrees. Exam Tip: one longitude E and one W means add the two values.

fib.questionText: A speed of one nautical mile per hour is called one ____.
fib.explanation: One knot is defined as a speed of one nautical mile per hour. Exam Tip: knots measure speed at sea, in nautical miles per hour.

fib.questionText: Two points on the same meridian have a latitude difference of 12 degrees. The distance between them is ____ nautical miles.
fib.explanation: A meridian is a great circle, so distance = 60 x latitude difference = 60 x 12 = 720 nautical miles. Exam Tip: on any great circle, multiply the angle in degrees by 60 to get nautical miles.

fib.questionText: Since cos 0 degrees = 1, the radius of the parallel at the equator equals ____.
fib.explanation: The radius of a parallel is R cos theta, and at the equator theta = 0 so R cos 0 = R x 1 = R. Exam Tip: the equator has the full radius R because cos 0 = 1.

fib.questionText: Longitudes are measured east or west of the ____ meridian.
fib.explanation: Longitude is measured from the prime meridian, also called the Greenwich meridian, which is at 0 degrees. Exam Tip: the prime meridian at 0 degrees is the starting line for longitude.

fib.questionText: The latitude difference between (35 degrees N, 20 degrees E) and (35 degrees S, 20 degrees E) is ____.
fib.explanation: The points are on opposite sides of the equator, so add the latitudes: 35 + 35 = 70 degrees. Exam Tip: one place N and one place S means add the latitudes.

tf.questionText: The equator is a great circle.
tf.explanation: The equator shares the same centre and radius as the earth, which is exactly the condition for a great circle.

tf.questionText: All parallels of latitude are great circles.
tf.explanation: Only the equator is a great circle; all other parallels of latitude are small circles because their centres are not the earth's centre.

tf.questionText: Every meridian of longitude is half of a great circle.
tf.explanation: A meridian and its opposite meridian together form a complete great circle passing through both poles, so each meridian is half of one.

tf.questionText: One degree of arc along a great circle corresponds to 60 nautical miles.
tf.explanation: One nautical mile is one minute of arc and there are 60 minutes in a degree, so one degree equals 60 nautical miles.

tf.questionText: The radius of the circle of latitude theta is R cos theta.
tf.explanation: The radius of a parallel of latitude is found by projecting the earth's radius, giving R cos theta.

tf.questionText: Longitude values range from 0 degrees to 360 degrees.
tf.explanation: Longitude ranges from 0 degrees to 180 degrees east or west of the prime meridian, not 0 to 360 degrees.

tf.questionText: Two places on the same meridian differ only in latitude.
tf.explanation: Points on the same meridian share the same longitude, so only their latitudes can differ.

tf.questionText: The distance along a parallel of latitude theta uses the factor sin theta.
tf.explanation: Distance along a parallel uses the factor cos theta, not sin theta, because the radius of the parallel is R cos theta.

tf.questionText: Latitude values range from 0 degrees to 90 degrees north or south.
tf.explanation: Latitude is measured from 0 degrees at the equator up to 90 degrees at each pole, north or south.

tf.questionText: The Greenwich meridian has longitude 0 degrees.
tf.explanation: The Greenwich or prime meridian is the reference line for longitude and is defined as 0 degrees.

summary.correctAnswer: The angular distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured from 0 degrees to 90 degrees.
summary.explanation: Latitude tells you how far a place is from the equator and is the first coordinate written in a position. Exam Tip: latitude uses N or S and is written before longitude.

summary.correctAnswer: The angular distance of a place east or west of the prime meridian, measured from 0 degrees to 180 degrees.
summary.explanation: Longitude tells you how far a place is from the Greenwich meridian and is the second coordinate in a position. Exam Tip: longitude uses E or W and is written after latitude.

summary.correctAnswer: The great circle at latitude 0 degrees that divides the earth into the northern and southern hemispheres.
summary.explanation: The equator is the reference from which latitude is measured and is the only parallel that is a great circle. Exam Tip: the equator is both latitude 0 degrees and a great circle.

summary.correctAnswer: The meridian at longitude 0 degrees from which all longitudes are measured east and west.
summary.explanation: The prime meridian passes through Greenwich and is the starting line for longitude. Exam Tip: longitude 0 degrees is always the prime meridian.

summary.correctAnswer: A circle on the sphere whose centre and radius are the same as those of the earth.
summary.explanation: The equator and all meridian circles are great circles, and the shortest distance between two points on the sphere lies on a great circle. Exam Tip: distances in nautical miles use great circles at 60 nm per degree.

summary.correctAnswer: A circle of latitude, parallel to the equator, whose centre is not the centre of the earth.
summary.explanation: All parallels of latitude except the equator are small circles with radius R cos theta. Exam Tip: every parallel except the equator is a small circle.

summary.correctAnswer: The distance along a great circle that subtends an angle of one minute of arc at the centre of the earth.
summary.explanation: Because one degree equals 60 minutes, one degree of arc on a great circle equals 60 nautical miles. Exam Tip: distance in nm = 60 x angle in degrees on a great circle.

summary.correctAnswer: A unit of speed equal to one nautical mile per hour.
summary.explanation: Knots measure the speed of ships and aircraft, where time = distance in nautical miles / speed in knots. Exam Tip: knots are nautical miles per hour, not km per hour.

summary.questionText: Radius of a parallel of latitude
summary.correctAnswer: The radius of a circle of latitude theta, given by R cos theta where R is the earth's radius.
summary.explanation: Since cos decreases from the equator to the poles, parallels get smaller as latitude increases. Exam Tip: use radius = R cos(latitude), and at the equator this equals R.

summary.correctAnswer: The arc length between two points on a great circle, equal to (theta/360) x 2 x pi x R in km or 60 x theta in nautical miles.
summary.explanation: Meridians and the equator are great circles, so distances along them use the full radius R. Exam Tip: for great-circle distance use (theta/360) x 40,040 km or 60 x theta nm.

hoq.questionText: Find the distance in km between A(40 degrees N, 25 degrees E) and B(10 degrees S, 25 degrees E). (Take 2 x pi x R = 40,040 km)
hoq.explanation: The points share the meridian 25 degrees E, so the path is along a great circle. They are on opposite sides of the equator, so add the latitudes: theta = 40 + 10 = 50 degrees. Distance = (theta/360) x 40,040 = (50/360) x 40,040 = 5,561.1 km. Exam Tip: on opposite sides of the equator you add the latitudes, giving 50 degrees, not 30 degrees.

hoq.questionText: Find the distance in km between P(60 degrees N, 20 degrees W) and Q(60 degrees N, 40 degrees E) along the parallel of latitude. (Take 2 x pi x R = 40,040 km)
hoq.explanation: The longitudes are on opposite sides of the prime meridian, so the longitude difference is 20 + 40 = 60 degrees. Distance along the parallel = (longitude difference / 360) x 40,040 x cos theta = (60/360) x 40,040 x cos 60 = (60/360) x 40,040 x 0.5 = 3,336.7 km. Exam Tip: for a parallel of latitude you must multiply by cos(latitude), here cos 60 = 0.5.

hoq.questionText: A ship leaves X(5 degrees N, 39 degrees E) and sails due south to Y(10 degrees S, 39 degrees E) at 25 knots. How long does the voyage take?
hoq.explanation: The ship stays on meridian 39 degrees E, a great circle, and crosses the equator, so the latitude difference is 5 + 10 = 15 degrees. Distance = 60 x 15 = 900 nautical miles. Time = distance / speed = 900 / 25 = 36 hours. Exam Tip: crossing the equator means adding the latitudes, giving 15 degrees.
